description: Digital marketing for real estate in Noida and Greater Noida: buyer targeting by corridor, UP RERA-safe ads and how to filter junk leads before they reach sales.
headline: Digital marketing for real estate in Noida: buyer targeting and lead quality
card_title: Digital marketing for real estate in Noida
card_text: Target Noida and Greater Noida buyers by corridor, keep ads UP RERA-safe and stop junk leads from eating your sales team's day.
intro:
Digital marketing for real estate in Noida has one problem that every developer and channel partner recognises: plenty of leads, not enough real buyers. A single launch on the Noida Expressway or in Greater Noida West can pull hundreds of form fills a week, and most sales teams spend their mornings calling wrong numbers, renters, people who "just filled the form" and buyers who already booked elsewhere.

This guide is about fixing that. It covers how Noida and Greater Noida buyers differ by corridor, how to keep your ads within UP RERA directions, how to build forms and pages that filter for intent, and which numbers tell you a campaign is working. If you sell in Gurugram as well, our Gurgaon micro-market playbook covers that side of the region.

sections.h2: Noida is four markets, not one
sections.html:
The first mistake in most Noida campaigns is targeting "Noida + 40 km" with one creative. A family upgrading from East Delhi, an IT professional renting near Sector 62 and an investor betting on the airport corridor want completely different things. Split your campaigns, landing pages and creatives by corridor.

CorridorWho usually enquiresWhat to lead with
Central Noida and the Sector 62 beltWorking professionals and families who want to live near offices and the MetroMetro access, ready or near-ready possession, schools and hospitals nearby
Noida Expressway (Sectors 94 to 168)Upgraders from Delhi and East Delhi, senior professionals, some NRIsDeveloper track record, specifications, green space, drive time to South Delhi
Greater Noida West (Noida Extension)First-time buyers and young families on a budgetPrice range, payment plan, possession date and proof of construction progress
Yamuna Expressway and the Jewar beltInvestors and plot buyers from across Delhi NCR and beyondPlots and approvals, distance to Noida International Airport, long-term infrastructure

Treat the table as a starting point. Within three or four weeks your own CRM will show which pin codes your booked site visits actually come from, and that data should replace any assumption here.

sections.h2: Keep every ad within UP RERA directions
sections.html:
Projects in Noida and Greater Noida are registered with the Uttar Pradesh Real Estate Regulatory Authority (UP RERA). Under the RERA Act a project must be registered before it is advertised or sold. UP RERA has also issued directions on advertising: the registration number and the UP RERA website should be shown clearly, and promoters have been told to print the project's QR code, which links to its registration details, on ads and brochures.

  • Registration number and QR code on every asset. Feed posts, Reels end cards, landing pages, brochures, hoardings and the WhatsApp auto-reply. On a small mobile ad, place them where they are readable, not hidden in a corner.
  • No pre-launch money. Avoid campaigns that collect EOI or booking amounts for a project that is not yet registered.
  • Claims that match the filing. Possession dates, amenities and tower counts should match what is registered. A buyer can scan the QR code and check.
  • No guaranteed-return promises. Commercial and retail units are often sold on rental yield. Promising fixed returns can attract regulatory trouble and ad rejections.

UP RERA updates its directions from time to time, so check the current rules on the UP RERA website and with your legal team before you launch.

sections.h2: Why Noida campaigns fill up with junk leads
sections.html:
Lead quality is the main reason Noida developers switch agencies. The causes are usually the same few things:

  • One-tap instant forms. Meta pre-fills name and phone, so people submit without reading. Many never remember doing it.
  • Broad targeting. "Interested in real estate" audiences include renters, brokers and students looking for PGs.
  • Price-led creatives. An ad that only shouts the lowest price attracts people whose budget is far below the actual unit cost.
  • Optimising for the wrong event. If the campaign optimises for form submits, Meta finds more people who submit forms, not people who visit sites.
  • Slow follow-up. A good lead called the next day often looks like a bad lead, because they have already spoken to three other projects.

Each of these has a fix, and none of them needs a bigger budget.

sections.h2: Build forms and pages that filter for intent
sections.html:
1. Use the higher-intent form type on Meta, which adds a review step before submitting.
  2. Ask two or three qualifying questions as multiple choice: budget band, configuration (2, 3 or 4 BHK, or plot), timeline (ready now, within a year, investment) and own use or investment. Keep it short; every extra question costs completions.
  3. Send serious traffic to a landing page with floor plans, price range, the UP RERA QR code, a map and a site visit booking button. People who spend a minute on that page are better buyers than people who tap a pre-filled form.
  4. Feed quality back to the platforms. Mark which leads were contacted, which visited and which booked, and send those events back through Meta's Conversions API and Google's offline conversion import. Over a few weeks the algorithms learn who your real buyers are.
  5. Remove what wastes money. Exclude existing leads, add negative keywords for rent, PG, resale and jobs, and drop placements that only send clicks.

This is the core of how our Facebook and Instagram ads team runs property campaigns: fewer leads, more people who actually turn up.

sections.h2: Google Search and YouTube for Noida buyers
sections.html:
Search captures people who already know what they want. In Noida those searches are very specific, so build tight ad groups around them:

  • Project and developer names, including spelling variations, so portals and resellers don't buy your own brand traffic.
  • Sector and configuration searches such as "3 BHK in Sector 150 Noida", "ready to move flats Noida Extension" or "plots on Yamuna Expressway".
  • Hindi and Hinglish searches, especially for Greater Noida West and Yamuna Expressway, where many buyers search as they speak.
  • Call tracking, since many buyers call straight from the ad rather than filling a form.

YouTube works well for walkthroughs and construction updates. A monthly drone or site video answers the most common Noida Extension question, "is the project actually being built?", better than any brochure. A Google Ads agency should connect call and site visit tracking before scaling spend.

sections.h2: Earn trust before the site visit
sections.html:
Many Noida and Greater Noida buyers have heard of delayed projects and registry problems in the region, and some have lived through them. Trust is a bigger lever here than discounts.

  • Show progress, not renders. Dated photos and videos of the actual towers, posted every month on Instagram, YouTube and the landing page.
  • Answer the hard questions upfront. Possession timeline, OC status for ready projects, registry process and maintenance charges. Put them in an FAQ on the project page.
  • Build reviews where buyers look. Ask buyers who have visited or booked to review your sales office or site on Google. Our guide to getting more Google reviews explains how to ask without breaking Google's rules.
  • Use real faces. A short video of your site engineer or sales head explaining the project builds more confidence than a voiceover.

sections.h2: Follow up within minutes, then measure the right numbers
sections.html:
In Noida, buyers compare several projects in the same week. Set clear follow-up targets: a WhatsApp reply with the brochure, location pin and RERA details within a minute; a human call within 15 minutes during working hours; and two specific site visit slots offered on the first call. Collect clear consent on forms, and check how India's data protection rules apply to your lead handling as their obligations phase in.

Then judge campaigns by what happens after the lead:

NumberHow to work it outWhat it tells you
Contact rateLeads reached on call ÷ total leadsFake numbers and slow follow-up
Qualified lead rateLeads matching budget and timeline ÷ leads reachedWhether targeting and forms are filtering
Cost per site visitAd spend ÷ completed site visitsThe number that predicts sales
Cost per bookingAd spend ÷ bookingsWhether to scale the campaign

Review these weekly by corridor and by campaign. Cut budgets on cost per site visit, never on cost per lead alone.

sections.h2: A 30-day plan for a Noida project
sections.html:
1. Week 1: one landing page per project with the UP RERA number and QR code, floor plans, price range, map, progress video and a site visit button. Set up call, form, WhatsApp and offline conversion tracking.
  2. Week 2: launch Meta higher-intent forms with qualifying questions for each corridor, and Google Search on project, sector and configuration keywords.
  3. Week 3: add remarketing to video viewers and page visitors, start sending contacted and visited leads back to Meta and Google, and add Hindi creatives if your buyers respond to them.
  4. Week 4: compare cost per site visit by campaign and corridor, pause the weakest third and move budget to what produced visits.

We run this as a 90-day sprint for property businesses across Delhi NCR from our office in Dwarka. See how we work as a digital marketing agency in Delhi NCR, or read the regional basics in our Delhi NCR real estate lead generation guide.

faqs: How do I get genuine real estate leads in Noida?

Use Meta's higher-intent lead forms with two or three qualifying questions, send serious traffic to a project landing page, run Google Search on project and sector keywords, and send contacted and visited leads back to Meta and Google so they learn who your real buyers are.
Do Noida property ads need the UP RERA QR code?

UP RERA has directed promoters to show the project's registration number, the UP RERA website and its QR code in advertisements and brochures. Directions change from time to time, so check the current rules on the UP RERA website before launching.
Is Greater Noida West marketed differently from the Noida Expressway?

Yes. Greater Noida West buyers are often first-time buyers watching price, payment plans and construction progress. Expressway buyers are usually upgraders who care more about the developer's track record, specifications and drive time to Delhi.
Why are my real estate leads from Facebook so poor in Noida?

Usually because of pre-filled instant forms, broad interest targeting, price-only creatives, optimising for form submits instead of site visits, and slow follow-up. Fix the form, the targeting and the reply time before raising the budget.
